title: Rescaling and clearing denominators before forming the delocalized quotient
statement: Let $R,A,\Lambda$ be commutative rings, with $A$ and $\Lambda$ algebras over $R$, and let $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ be an $R$-algebra homomorphism. Let $S\subset R$ be a multiplicative submonoid and use localization at its images [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Fix nonnegative integers $n,t,m,c$ with $c\le n+m$, and a presentation $P$ of $A$ with generators $p_i$ ($i\in\operatorname{Fin}n$), relations $g_j\in R[x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}]$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}t$), and kernel generated by these relations [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $D$ be an $S^{-1}R$-algebra, $Q$ a standard smooth presentation of $D$ with $n+m$ variables and $c$ relations whose initial Jacobian minor is a unit [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], and $S^{-1}A\xrightarrow{\beta}D\xrightarrow{\gamma}S^{-1}\Lambda$ a factorization of $S^{-1}\alpha$. Suppose that the first $n$ variables of $Q$ represent $\beta(p_i/1)$. Put $T=R[x_0,\ldots,x_{n+m-1}]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], write $\widetilde g_j$ for $g_j$ with variables included as the first $n$, and use polynomial partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. Then there exist polynomials $f_j\in T$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}c$), elements $l_i\in\Lambda$ ($i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n+m)$), $s_0\in S$, $a_0,a_j\in T$, and $sg_j\in S$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}t$), $sf_j\in S$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}c$), such that $l_i=\alpha(p_i)$ for $i<n$, $C(s_0)=a_0\Delta(f)+\sum_{j<c}a_jf_j$, $C(sg_j)\widetilde g_j\in(f_0,\ldots,f_{c-1})$ for every $j<t$, and $\operatorname{ev}_l(C(sf_j)f_j)=0$ for every $j<c$. Here $C:R\to T$ is the constant inclusion and $\Delta(f)=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j<c}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), proof

proof.text: Use hfactor and hval to identify gamma(Q.val_i) with alpha(P.val_i)/1 for the first n variables. Apply the rescaled-integral-presentation theorem, which constructs integral equations f_j, generators z_i of D, and lifts l_i in Lambda with the first n generators fixed, the evaluation kernel generated by map(f_j), and the evaluated minor a unit.

Let delta be the initial minor and J the ideal generated by delta and the f_j in T=R[X]. Localize T at the constants from S using MvPolynomial.isLocalization. Lift the inverse of the evaluated minor along the surjective evaluation map. The polynomial b*map(delta)-1 belongs to the evaluation kernel, hence to the mapped ideal J. Also b*map(delta) belongs to that ideal, so subtraction gives 1 in the mapped ideal J. IsLocalization.algebraMap_mem_map_algebraMap_iff gives s0 in S with C(s0) in J, without an injectivity assumption. Ideal.mem_span_insert and mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun give the required exact determinant certificate.

Evaluation at z of each renamed relation of P vanishes: on constants the evaluation agrees with beta composed with localization of the original evaluation by scalar-tower compatibility, and on variables it agrees by the fixed-generator property and hval. Therefore each renamed relation belongs after coefficient extension to the mapped ideal generated by f. Apply the same ideal localization membership criterion to obtain sg_j in S with C(sg_j) times that relation in the original ideal.

The image in L of the evaluation at l of each f_j is zero, because gamma(z_i)=l_i/1 and f_j belongs to the evaluation kernel in D. The equality of these polynomial evaluations follows by induction on constants, addition, and multiplication by variables; constants use the two scalar towers into L. IsLocalization.map_eq_zero_iff supplies a denominator in the image of S in Lambda. Pull it back to an element sf_j of S to obtain the required zero evaluation. Choose the finite families sg and sf and assemble the witnesses and all four conclusions.
